sentences.zh: 卿又云：守宰貪殘，皆由滋味過度。

translations.literal: You also say: "Governors' greed and cruelty all come from excessive delicacies."
translations.idiomatic: You also say, "Local greed and cruelty all come from extravagant food."

sentences.zh: 貪殘糜費，已如前答。

translations.literal: Greed, cruelty, and wasteful spending—I have already answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: On greed, cruelty, and waste I have already replied.

sentences.zh: 漢文雖愛露臺之產，鄧通之錢布於天下，以此而治，朕無愧焉。

translations.literal: Han Wendi though he loved the terrace crop, Deng Tong's coin spread through the realm—with such governance I have no shame.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi loved his terrace garden and Deng Tong's wealth filled the realm. I rule no worse and feel no shame.

sentences.zh: 若以下民飲食過差，亦復不然。

translations.literal: As for common people's food overstepping bounds—that too is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Nor is it true that commoners eat beyond their station.

sentences.zh: 天監之初，思之已甚。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianjian I thought on this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: I considered this carefully at the beginning of Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 其勤力營產，則無不富饒；

translations.literal: Those who labor to build property are without exception rich;
translations.idiomatic: Those who work hard prosper;

sentences.zh: 惰游緩事，則家業貧窶。

translations.literal: the idle and slack in affairs end in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: the idle and careless grow poor.

sentences.zh: 勤修產業，以營盤案，自己營之，自己食之，何損於天下？

translations.literal: Diligently manage property and set the table—oneself earn it, oneself eat it: what harm to the realm?
translations.idiomatic: A man who builds his estate and eats what he earns—how does that harm the realm?

sentences.zh: 無賴子弟，惰營產業，致於貧窶，無可施設，此何益於天下？

translations.literal: Good-for-nothing sons who idly neglect property end in poverty with nothing to deploy—what benefit to the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Wastrels who neglect their fields end penniless and useless—what good is that to the realm?

sentences.zh: 且又意雖曰同富，富有不同：慳而富者，終不能設；

translations.literal: And though one may speak of "equal wealth," wealth differs: the stingy rich can never deploy;
translations.idiomatic: You speak as if all wealth were the same, but it is not. The miser may be rich yet can do nothing with it;

sentences.zh: 奢而富者，于事何損？

translations.literal: the lavish rich—what harm to affairs?
translations.idiomatic: the spendthrift rich—what injury do they do the state?

sentences.zh: 若使朝廷緩其刑，此事終不可斷；

translations.literal: If the court eases punishments, this can never be ended;
translations.idiomatic: Relax the law and excess will never end;

sentences.zh: 若急其制，則曲屋密房之中，云何可知？

translations.literal: if it tightens regulation, then inside curved chambers and hidden rooms—how can one know?
translations.idiomatic: tighten it and who can see what happens behind closed doors?

sentences.zh: 若家家搜檢，其細已甚，欲使吏不呼門，其可得乎？

translations.literal: If every house is searched, the minutiae become extreme—wish clerks never to knock at doors: can this be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Search every home and the scrutiny becomes unbearable. You want officials never to knock on a door—is that possible?

sentences.zh: 更相恐脅，以求財帛，足長禍萌，無益治道。

translations.literal: Mutual intimidation to extract coin only lengthens the sprouts of disaster and benefits governance not at all.
translations.idiomatic: Men threatening one another for money only breed worse trouble. That is no way to govern.

sentences.zh: 若以此指朝廷，我無此事。

translations.literal: If by this you mean the court—I have no such matter.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean the court by this, I know nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 昔之牲牢，久不宰殺，朝中會同，菜蔬而已，意粗得奢約之節。

translations.literal: Formerly sacrificial beasts went long unslaughtered; court gatherings had only vegetables—I roughly grasped the measure of splendor and thrift.
translations.idiomatic: For years we ceased slaughtering for sacrifice. Court feasts were vegetables only. I thought I had found a fair balance of frugality and dignity.

sentences.zh: 若復減此，必有《蟋蟀》之譏。

translations.literal: If this is reduced further, there will surely be the reproach of the "Cricket."
translations.idiomatic: Cut more and you will invite the reproach of the "Cricket."

sentences.zh: 若以爲功德事者，皆是園中之所產育。

translations.literal: If you think merit affairs—all are bred in the imperial gardens.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean Buddhist merit works, their food comes from the palace gardens.

sentences.zh: 功德之事，亦無多費，變一瓜爲數十種，食一菜爲數十味，不變瓜菜，亦無多種，以變故多，何損於事，亦豪芥不關國家。

translations.literal: Merit affairs also cost little: one melon into dozens of kinds, one dish into dozens of flavors; without changing melon or vegetable there are not many kinds—because of variety, what harm to affairs? It touches the state not in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Even merit feasts cost little. One melon becomes a dozen dishes, one vegetable a dozen flavors—yet without artifice there are few kinds. What harm is there in variety? It does not touch the state at all.

sentences.zh: 如得財如法而用，此不愧乎人。

translations.literal: To obtain wealth and use it lawfully—this is no shame before men.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth lawfully gained and lawfully spent is nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 我自除公宴，不食國家之食，多歷年稔，乃至宮人，亦不食國家之食，積累歲月。

translations.literal: I myself, apart from public feasts, do not eat the state's food—many years; even palace women do not eat state food—months piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from state banquets I have not eaten public rations for many years, and even the palace women have gone without them for a long time.

sentences.zh: 凡所營造，不關材官，及以國匠，皆資雇借，以成其事。

translations.literal: All construction does not involve the materials office or state artisans—all is hired on loan to complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: Every building project avoids the materials bureau and state craftsmen. I hire labor and pay for the work myself.

sentences.zh: 近之得財，頗有方便，民得其利，國得其利，我得其利，營諸功德。

translations.literal: Recent income has had convenient paths—the people gain, the state gains, I gain, and merit works are built.
translations.idiomatic: Money lately raised has served everyone: the people profit, the state profits, I profit, and merit works are funded.

sentences.zh: 或以卿之心度我之心，故不能得知。

translations.literal: Perhaps you measure my heart by your heart and therefore cannot know.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps you judge me by yourself, and that is why you do not understand.

sentences.zh: 所得財用，暴於天下，不得曲辭辯論。

translations.literal: Income obtained is displayed to the realm—no twisting words in debate.
translations.idiomatic: What I receive is open to the world. Do not argue in evasions.

sentences.zh: 卿又云女妓越濫，此有司之責，雖然，亦有不同：貴者多畜妓樂，至於勳附若兩掖，亦復不聞家有二八，多畜女妓者。

translations.literal: You also say female entertainers overflow—this is the responsible officials' duty; still there are differences: the noble mostly keep music girls, but even merit lords and the two flanks—one does not hear of households with "two-eight," or of many keeping female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: You also complain that courtesans are too many. That is the censors' business, though the cases differ. The great mostly keep musicians, but even meritorious lords and the two palace wings—one seldom hears of a household keeping "two-eight" girls or hoarding courtesans.

sentences.zh: 此並宜具言其人，當令有司振其霜豪。

translations.literal: These should all be named; let the offices shake off their frost and pride.
translations.idiomatic: Name every offender. Let the responsible offices strip away their arrogance.

sentences.zh: 卿又云：「乃追恨所取爲少，如復傅翼，增其搏噬，一何悖哉。

translations.literal: You also say: "Yet they regret what they took was little; if given wings again, increasing their tearing and devouring—how perverse!"
translations.idiomatic: You also wrote: "They regret having taken too little, and if given wings again they tear all the harder—how perverse!"

sentences.zh: 」勇怯不同，貪廉各用，勇者可使進取，怯者可使守城，貪者可使捍禦，廉者可使牧民。

translations.literal: Bravery and timidity differ; greed and integrity each have their use—the brave may be sent to attack, the timid to hold cities, the greedy to defend the frontier, the upright to rule the people.
translations.idiomatic: Courage and cowardice are not the same, nor are greed and integrity. Use the brave for advance, the timid for defense, the greedy for the border, the honest for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 向使叔齊守于西河，豈能濟事？

translations.literal: Had Bo Yi alone guarded the western river, could the affair have succeeded?
translations.idiomatic: If Bo Yi alone had held the western river, would anything have been accomplished?

sentences.zh: 吳起育民，必無成功。

translations.literal: Wu Qi nurturing the people would surely have had no success.
translations.idiomatic: If Wu Qi had only nurtured the people, he would never have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 若使吳起而不重用，則西河之功廢。

translations.literal: If Wu Qi had not been heavily employed, the achievement at the western river would have been wasted.
translations.idiomatic: Had Wu Qi not been used as he deserved, the western river would never have been won.

sentences.zh: 今之文武，亦復如此。

translations.literal: Today's civil and military officers are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same is true of civil and military men today.

sentences.zh: 取其搏噬之用，不能得不重更任，彼亦非爲朝廷爲之傅翼。

translations.literal: Take their tearing and devouring use—they cannot but be heavily employed again; the court did not give them wings for that purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Use their predatory talents and you cannot avoid employing them heavily again. The court did not give them wings so they could prey harder.

sentences.zh: 卿以朝廷爲悖，乃自甘之，當思致悖所以。

translations.literal: You call the court perverse yet willingly serve it—you should consider what makes perversity.
translations.idiomatic: You call the court perverse yet still serve it willingly. Ask yourself what makes it perverse.

sentences.zh: 卿云「宜導之以節儉」。

translations.literal: You say, "One should guide them with thrift."
translations.idiomatic: You say, "They should be guided by frugality."

sentences.zh: 又云「至治者必以淳素爲先」。

translations.literal: And, "Supreme rule must take plain simplicity first."
translations.idiomatic: And, "Perfect government begins in plain simplicity."

sentences.zh: 此言大善。

translations.literal: These words are very fine.
translations.idiomatic: That is well said.

sentences.zh: 夫子言「其身正，不令而行；

translations.literal: The Master said, "If his person is upright, without being ordered it is done;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "When the ruler's person is upright, things are done though he does not command;

sentences.zh: 其身不正，雖令不從」。

translations.literal: if his person is not upright, though ordered they do not follow."
translations.idiomatic: when his person is not upright, they will not obey though he commands."

sentences.zh: 朕絕房室三十餘年，無有淫佚。

translations.literal: I have cut off the inner chambers for thirty-odd years—no licentiousness.
translations.idiomatic: I have kept no harem for more than thirty years and have known no debauchery.

sentences.zh: 朕頗自計，不與女人同屋而寢，亦三十餘年。

translations.literal: I count myself: not sleeping in the same room with women—also thirty-odd years.
translations.idiomatic: By my own reckoning I have not slept in the same room with a woman for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 至於居處不過一床之地，雕飾之物不入于宮，此亦人所共知。

translations.literal: My dwelling is no more than one bed's space; carved ornament never enters the palace—this too all know.
translations.idiomatic: My living space is no larger than a bed. Ornament does not enter the palace. Everyone knows this.

sentences.zh: 受生不飲酒，受生不好音聲，所以朝中曲宴，未嘗奏樂，此羣賢之所觀見。

translations.literal: Since birth I do not drink; since birth I dislike sound—so at court informal feasts music is never played; the worthies have seen this.
translations.idiomatic: I have never drunk and never cared for music, so at court gatherings no instruments are played. The ministers have seen it themselves.

sentences.zh: 朕三更出理事，隨事多少，事少或中前得竟，或事多至日昃方得就食。

translations.literal: I rise at the third watch to handle affairs; as affairs vary—few affairs and I may finish before noon; many affairs and only at sundown may I eat.
translations.idiomatic: I rise in the deep night to work. When business is light I may finish before noon. When it is heavy I eat only after the sun has slanted west.

sentences.zh: 日常一食，若晝若夜，無有定時。

translations.literal: Usually one meal, day or night, at no fixed hour.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule I eat once, by day or night, at no set time.

sentences.zh: 疾苦之日，或亦再食。

translations.literal: On days of illness, sometimes two meals.
translations.idiomatic: When I am ill I may eat twice.

sentences.zh: 昔要腹過於十圍，今之瘦削裁二尺餘，舊帶猶存，非爲妄說。

translations.literal: Once my waist was more than ten girths; now I am wasted to barely two feet odd—the old belt still kept; this is no empty claim.
translations.idiomatic: Once my belly measured more than ten spans around. Now I am scarcely two feet about the waist. The old belt is still here. I do not lie.

sentences.zh: 爲誰爲之？

translations.literal: For whom was it done?
translations.idiomatic: For whom did I do this?

sentences.zh: 救物故也。

translations.literal: To save the creatures—that is why.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the living—that is why.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。

translations.literal: The Documents say, "Limbs and arms are the man; good ministers make the sage."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "Arms and legs are the man; worthy ministers make the sage."

sentences.zh: 」向使朕有股肱，故可得中主。

translations.literal: Had I such limbs and arms, I could have been a middling lord.
translations.idiomatic: Had I such ministers, I might have been a passable ruler.

sentences.zh: 今乃不免居九品之下，「不令而行」，徒虛言耳。

translations.literal: Now I still cannot rise above the ninth grade—"without being ordered it is done" is only empty words.
translations.idiomatic: As it is I remain no better than the lowest grade of ruler. "Without being ordered it is done" is only an empty phrase.

sentences.zh: 卿今慊言，便罔知所答。

translations.literal: You now speak fully—at once I do not know what to answer.
translations.idiomatic: You press your case so hard that I scarcely know how to reply.

sentences.zh: 卿又云「百司莫不奏事，詭競求進」。

translations.literal: You also say, "The hundred offices all memorialize, deviously competing for advancement."
translations.idiomatic: You also say, "Every office memorializes, scheming for promotion."

sentences.zh: 此又是誰？

translations.literal: Who are these again?
translations.idiomatic: Who are they? Name them.

sentences.zh: 何者復是詭事？

translations.literal: Which affairs again are the deceptive matters?
translations.idiomatic: Which are these deceptive affairs again?

sentences.zh: 今不使外人呈事，於義可否？

translations.literal: Now not to let outsiders present affairs—in principle is that permissible?
translations.idiomatic: If outsiders may no longer present memorials, is that right in principle?

sentences.zh: 無人廢職，職可廢乎？

translations.literal: Without men offices are abandoned—can offices be abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: No men, no offices—can you abolish the offices themselves?

sentences.zh: 職廢則人亂，人亂則國安乎？

translations.literal: Offices abandoned, then men are confused; men confused, then is the state at peace?
translations.idiomatic: Abolish offices and men fall into disorder; men in disorder—and the realm is secure?

sentences.zh: 以咽廢飧，此之謂也。

translations.literal: To reject food because of the throat—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Reject the meal because the throat hurts—that is the case.

sentences.zh: 若斷呈事，誰屍其任？

translations.literal: If presenting affairs is cut off, who bears the responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: Cut off memorials—who then answers for the charge?

sentences.zh: 專委之人，云何可得？

translations.literal: Men exclusively entrusted—how can they be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Where will you find men fit to be trusted with everything alone?

sentences.zh: 是故古人云：「專聽生姦，獨任成亂。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said: "Exclusive listening breeds treachery; sole trust breeds chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said it plainly: "Listen to one voice and treachery is born; trust one man alone and chaos follows.

sentences.zh: 」猶二世之委趙高，元後之付王莽。

translations.literal: " Just as Er Shi entrusted Zhao Gao, and Yuandi's successor entrusted Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Think of Er Shi handing everything to Zhao Gao, or Yuandi's heir giving the realm to Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 呼鹿爲馬，卒有閻樂望夷之禍，王莽亦終移漢鼎。

translations.literal: Calling a deer a horse—in the end came the disaster of Yan Le at Wangyi; Wang Mang also finally moved the tripod of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Call a deer a horse, and in the end Yan Le brings ruin at Wangyi; Wang Mang too shifts the Han throne from its base.

sentences.zh: 卿云「吹毛求疵」，復是何人所吹之疵？

translations.literal: You say "splitting hairs for flaws"—again, whose flaws are being split?
translations.idiomatic: You wrote "splitting hairs for flaws"—whose flaws? Name him.

sentences.zh: 「擘肌分理」，復是何人乎？

translations.literal: "Splitting muscle to distinguish principle"—again, who is it?
translations.idiomatic: "Splitting muscle to distinguish principle"—who is that?

sentences.zh: 事及「深刻」「繩逐」，並復是誰？

translations.literal: Matters touching "severity" and "driving by the cord"—again, who are they?
translations.idiomatic: When you speak of "severity" and "driving by the cord," who are they?

sentences.zh: 又云「治、署、邸、肆」，何者宜除？

translations.literal: You also say "administration, offices, lodges, markets"—which ought to be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: You also named "bureaus, offices, lodges, markets"—which should be abolished?

sentences.zh: 何者宜省？

translations.literal: Which ought to be reduced?
translations.idiomatic: Which should be cut?

sentences.zh: 「國容戎備」，何者宜省？

translations.literal: "State display and military preparedness"—which ought to be reduced?
translations.idiomatic: "State ceremony and armaments"—what should be trimmed?

sentences.zh: 何者未須？

translations.literal: Which are not yet needed?
translations.idiomatic: What is not needed now?

sentences.zh: 「四方屯傳」，何者無益？

translations.literal: "Relay posts in all four quarters"—which are useless?
translations.idiomatic: "Garrisons and relays in all four quarters"—which do no good?

sentences.zh: 何者妨民？

translations.literal: Which harm the people?
translations.idiomatic: Which harm the people?

sentences.zh: 何處興造而是役民？

translations.literal: Where is construction that conscripts the people?
translations.idiomatic: Where do you build at the cost of forced labor?

sentences.zh: 何處費財而是非急？

translations.literal: Where is wealth spent on what is not urgent?
translations.idiomatic: Where is treasure spent on what is not urgent?

sentences.zh: 若爲「討召」？

translations.literal: As for "summons and recruitment"?
translations.idiomatic: What of "summons and recruitment"?

sentences.zh: 若爲「征賦」？

translations.literal: As for "levies and requisitions"?
translations.idiomatic: What of "levies and requisitions"?

sentences.zh: 朝廷從來無有此事，靜息之方復何者？

translations.literal: The court has never had such matters from the beginning—what methods quiet and rest them?
translations.idiomatic: The court has never done such things. What is your plan to bring them to rest?

sentences.zh: 宜各出其事，具以奏聞。

translations.literal: Each should state the affair and memorialize it in full.
translations.idiomatic: Let each charge be named and reported in full.

sentences.zh: 卿云「若不及于時大息其民，事至方圖，知無及也」。

translations.literal: You say, "If one does not at this time greatly rest the people, and only plans when the affair has arrived, one knows it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: You wrote, "Fail now to give the people real rest, and plan only when crisis comes—you will know you are already too late."

sentences.zh: 如卿此言，卽時便是大役其民，是何處所？

translations.literal: By your words, at this very moment you are greatly overworking the people—where is that?
translations.idiomatic: By your own logic you are overworking the people right now—where?

sentences.zh: 卿云「國弊民疲」，誠如卿言，終須出其事，不得空作漫語。

translations.literal: You say "the state is spent and the people weary"—if it is truly as you say, in the end you must state the affairs; you cannot make empty, roaming words.
translations.idiomatic: You say "the realm is hollow and the people exhausted." If that is so, name the facts. Do not speak in empty generalities.

sentences.zh: 夫能言之，必能行之。

translations.literal: One who can speak of it must be able to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Who can talk must also act.

sentences.zh: 富國強兵之術，急民省役之宜，號令遠近之法，並宜具列。

translations.literal: Methods to enrich the state and strengthen the army, measures urgent for resting the people and reducing corvée, commands for the near and far—all should be listed in full.
translations.idiomatic: Ways to enrich the state and strengthen the army, plans to spare the people and cut corvée, orders for near and far—list them all.

sentences.zh: 若不具列，則是欺罔朝廷，空示頰舌。

translations.literal: If you do not list them in full, then you are deceiving the court and showing only cheek and tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Fail to list them and you deceive the throne with nothing but lip service.

sentences.zh: 凡人有爲，先須內省，惟無瑕者，可以戮人。

translations.literal: Whenever a man would act, he must first look inward; only one without flaw may punish others.
translations.idiomatic: Before you judge others, judge yourself. Only the spotless may sit in judgment.

sentences.zh: 卿不得曆詆內外，而不極言其事。

translations.literal: You may not go through the court inside and out with slander and not speak to the utmost of the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: You may not slander everyone within and without the palace and still refuse to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 佇聞重奏，當復省覽，付之尚書，班下海內，庶亂羊永除，害馬長息，惟新之美，復見今日。

translations.literal: I await hearing your further memorial; I shall again examine it, entrust it to the Masters of Writing, and promulgate it within the four seas—so that bad sheep may be forever removed, harmful horses long stilled, and the beauty of renewal appear again today.
translations.idiomatic: I await your next memorial. I shall read it again, send it to the Masters of Writing, and publish it throughout the realm—so the bad sheep are driven off, the harmful horse stilled, and renewal shines once more.

sentences.zh: 琛奉敕，但謝過而已，不敢復有指斥。

translations.literal: Chen received the edict and only apologized, not daring to criticize again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen took the edict and could only apologize. He did not dare remonstrate again.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷太府卿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Minister of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made Minister of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，遷雲騎將軍、中軍宣城王長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to General of the Cloud Cavalry and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Xuancheng, Commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he became General of the Cloud Cavalry and chief clerk to the Prince of Xuancheng, commander of the central army.

sentences.zh: 侯景舉兵襲京師，王移入臺內，留琛與司馬楊曒守東府。

translations.literal: Hou Jing raised troops and struck the capital; the prince moved into the inner palace, leaving Chen and the marshal Yang Xun to hold the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing marched on the capital the prince withdrew into the inner palace and left Chen and Marshal Yang Xun to defend the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 賊尋攻陷城，放兵殺害，琛被槍未至死，賊求得之，轝至闕下，求見僕射王克、領軍朱异，勸開城納賊。

translations.literal: The rebels soon stormed the city, let their soldiers slaughter, and Chen was speared but not killed; the rebels found him, carried him in a litter to the palace gate, and sought audience with Vice Director Wang Ke and Commander of the Army Zhu Yi, urging them to open the city and admit the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon broke the city and unleashed slaughter. Chen was speared but lived. They found him, bore him in a litter to the palace gate, and demanded Wang Ke, Vice Director, and Zhu Yi, Commander of the Army, begging them to open the gates to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 克等讓之，涕泣而止，賊復轝送莊嚴寺療治之。

translations.literal: Ke and the others rebuked him; weeping, he stopped, and the rebels again carried him in a litter to Zhuangyan Monastery for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke and the others reproached him until he wept and fell silent. The rebels carried him back to Zhuangyan Monastery to heal his wounds.

sentences.zh: 明年，臺城不守，琛逃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: The next year the inner city could not be held; Chen fled home to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the inner city fell. Chen fled to his home district.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，賊進寇會稽，復執琛送出都，以爲金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels advanced against Kuaiji, seized Chen again, and sent him back to the capital, making him Household Counsellor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the rebels marched on Kuaiji, they seized Chen again and sent him to the capital as Household Counsellor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後遇疾卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: Later he fell ill and died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell ill and died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 琛所撰《三禮講疏》、《五經滯義》及諸儀法，凡百餘篇。

translations.literal: Chen compiled the Exegesis of the Three Rites, the Stalled Meanings of the Five Classics, and various ritual regulations—more than a hundred chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Exegesis of the Three Rites, the Stalled Meanings of the Five Classics, and many works on ritual—over a hundred chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 子詡，太清初，自儀同西昌侯掾，出爲巴山太守，在郡遇亂卒。

translations.literal: His son Xu, at the beginning of Taiqing, rose from aide to the Marquis of Xichang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, and went out as Administrator of Bashan; in the commandery he met with the chaos and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu, early in Taiqing, left a post as aide to the Marquis of Xichang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, to serve as Administrator of Bashan, and died there when rebellion swept the region.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察云：夏侯勝有言曰：「士患不明經術；

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: Xia Hou Sheng had a saying: "The gentleman's trouble is not knowing the classics;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: Xia Hou Sheng once said, "The scholar's trouble is not knowing the classics;

sentences.zh: 經術明，取青紫如拾地芥耳。

translations.literal: once the classics are clear, taking blue and purple is like picking up a mustard plant from the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Once the classics are clear, rank and office are like picking up a mustard plant from the ground."

sentences.zh: 」朱异、賀琛並起微賤，以經術逢時，致於貴顯，符其言矣。

translations.literal: " Zhu Yi and He Chen both rose from humble beginnings; by the classics they met their time and reached noble eminence—this matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi and He Chen both rose from humble beginnings; the classics brought them to high rank in their day—exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 而异遂徼寵倖，任事居權，不能以道佐君，苟取容媚。

translations.literal: Yet Yi went on to seek favor and fortune, hold office and wield power, and could not assist his lord by the Way but only sought to please and flatter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yi sought favor and power, held office, and could not guide his lord by the Way—only by pleasing and flattering.

sentences.zh: 及延寇敗國，實异之由。

translations.literal: When the rebel prolonged his ravaging of the state, the fault was truly Yi's.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel ravaged the realm, the blame was truly Yi's.

sentences.zh: 禍難旣彰，不明其罪，至於身死，寵贈猶殊。

translations.literal: Once disaster was plain, his guilt was not made clear; even at his death, favors and gifts were still extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Once disaster was plain his guilt went unnamed; even in death his honors were lavish.

sentences.zh: 罰旣弗加，賞亦斯濫，失於勸沮，何以爲國？

translations.literal: Punishment was not applied, reward likewise ran wild—failure in encouragement and restraint; how can such a thing be called a state?
translations.idiomatic: No punishment fell, rewards ran wild—how can a state encourage good and restrain evil like this?

sentences.zh: 君子是以知太清之亂，能無及是乎。

translations.literal: The gentleman therefore knows that the chaos of Taiqing could not fail to reach this.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman therefore knows that the chaos of Taiqing could not have stopped short of this.
